poetic_form.description: The Mother of Droplets is a poetic riddle concerning someone's character, originating in The Playful Dyes. The rules of the form are applied by poets to produce individual poems which can be recited. The poem is a single line. Use of simile is characteristic of the form. The poem has seven syllables.

The Poetic Skirt is a reflective poetic form concerning someone recently deceased, originating in The Playful Dyes. The rules of the form are applied by poets to produce individual poems which can be recited. The poem is divided into three distinct parts: a tercet, two couplets and another tercet. Use of consonance and symbolism is characteristic of the form. Each line has ten syllables. [B]The first part is intended to describe the subject of the poem. Certain lines sometimes have reversed word orders. The rhyme scheme respecting the full poem is ABB. [B]The second part is intended to develop the previous idea. The second line of each couplet reverses the word order of the first line. The rhyme scheme respecting the full poem is CC. [B]The third part is intended to make an apology. Certain lines sometimes have reversed word orders. The rhyme scheme within this stanza is abb.

The Sweet String is a poetic narrative concerning alcoholic beverages, originating in The Confederacy of Heart. The rules of the form are applied by poets to produce individual poems which can be recited. The poem is divided into three distinct parts: a quintain, another quintain and a line. Each line has ten syllables. Every line of the poem has a medial caesura. [B]The first part is intended to express grief over the subject of the poem. Certain lines sometimes have reversed word orders. The third line of the quintain has the same grammatical structure as the first line. [B]The second part is intended to reflect on previous ideas. Certain lines have similar grammatical structures. The fifth line of the quintain reverses the word order of the second line. [B]The third part is intended to offer a different perspective.

The Dyes of Turquoise is a poetic narrative intended to describe Luto the Aquamarine Steel, originating in The Confederacy of Heart. The rules of the form are applied by poets to produce individual poems which can be recited. The poem is three quatrains. Use of consonance and ambiguity is characteristic of the form. Each line has six syllables. The fourth line of each quatrain must expand the idea of the third line.

The Golden Esteem is a dramatic poetic form intended to teach a moral lesson concerning wind, originating in The Confederacy of Heart. The rules of the form are applied by poets to produce individual poems which can be recited. The poem is a series of quatrains. Forms of parallelism are common throughout the poem, in that certain lines are required to maintain phrasing and they reverse grammatical structures. Each line has eight syllables. Every line of the poem has an initial caesura. The second line of each quatrain uses the same placement of allusions as the first line. The third line of each quatrain presents a different view of the subject of the second line.

The Poetic Bewilderment is a poetic riddle concerning a specific place, originating in The Hex of Deceivers. The rules of the form are applied by poets to produce individual poems which can be recited. The poem is a single couplet. Use of metaphor and vivid imagery is characteristic of the form. Each line has six syllables. Every line of the poem has an initial caesura. The ending of each line of the poem shares the same rhyme. The first line is intended to express grief over the subject of the poem. The second line is intended to refuse consolation.

The Suitor of Berries is a poetic narrative intended to describe a historical figure, originating in The Hex of Deceivers. The rules of the form are applied by poets to produce individual poems which can be recited. The poem is a single line. Use of metaphor is characteristic of the form. The poem has seven syllables.

The Taupe Pages is a light poetic form intended to express pleasure with a specific place, originating in The Hex of Deceivers. The rules of the form are applied by poets to produce individual poems which can be recited. The poem is four to five tercets. Use of consonance and simile is characteristic of the form. The ending of each line of the poem shares the same rhyme.

The Monger of Ferries is a poetic riddle intended to express grief over family, originating in The Hex of Deceivers. The rules of the form are applied by poets to produce individual poems which can be recited. The poem is five tercets. Forms of parallelism are common throughout the poem, in that certain lines often share an underlying meaning and they have similar grammatical structures. Each line has five syllables. The third line of each tercet presents a different view of the subject of the first line. The rhyme scheme of the poem is ABA.

The Silk of Laces is a poetic form intended to express grief over a chosen subject, originating in The Hex of Deceivers. The rules of the form are applied by poets to produce individual poems which can be recited. The poem is a single tercet. Use of internal rhyme is characteristic of the form. A form of parallelism is common throughout the poem, in that certain lines often contrast underlying meaning. Each line has nine syllables. The ending of each line of the poem shares the same rhyme. The third line of the tercet presents a different view of the subject of the second line.

The Page of Pantomimes is a poetic riddle intended to express grief over current events, originating in The Responsible Apes. The form guides poets during improvised performances. The poem is a single quatrain. A form of parallelism is common throughout the poem, in that certain lines have similar grammatical structures. Each line has seven syllables. Every line of the poem has a medial caesura. The third line of the quatrain uses the same placement of allusions as the first line. The third line of the quatrain presents a different view of the subject of the first line. The second line must make use of juxtaposition. The third line must make use of juxtaposition. The rhyme scheme of the poem is AABA.

The Flax of Crabs is a dramatic poetic form intended to teach a moral lesson concerning the concept of nature, originating in The Responsible Apes. The rules of the form are applied by poets to produce individual poems which can be recited. The poem is a single tercet. Each line has eight syllables. The rules of the form are applied by poets to produce individual poems which can be recited. The poem is a single couplet. The ending of each line of the poem shares the same rhyme. The second line of the couplet must expand the idea of the first line. The first line is intended to make an assertion. It has six syllables. The second line is intended to invert the previous assertion. It has eight syllables.

The Cyclopean Oracle is a light poetic form concerning the future, originating in The Pointy Seduction. The rules of the form are applied by poets to produce individual poems which can be recited. The poem is a single couplet. Forms of parallelism are common throughout the poem, in that certain lines often share an underlying meaning, they use the same placement of allusions and they reverse grammatical structures. Each line has seven syllables. Every line of the poem has an initial caesura. The ending of each line of the poem shares the same rhyme. The first line is intended to express grief over the subject of the poem. The second line is intended to console the audience. It must make use of epenthesis and vivid imagery.

The Wooden Seasons is a dramatic poetic form intended to beseech Acithi the Rainy Vegetation originally devised by the elf Ada Tamebeard. The rules of the form are applied by poets to produce individual poems which can be recited. The poem is a single tercet. Use of consonance, symbolism and simile is characteristic of the form. The ending of each line of the poem shares the same rhyme. The first line has six syllables. The second line has six syllables. The third line has six syllables.

The Lyrical Lute is a light poetic form intended to describe a chosen subject originally devised by the goblin Ber Criedplagues. The form guides poets during improvised performances. The poem is a single couplet. Forms of parallelism are common throughout the poem, in that certain lines often share an underlying meaning and they sometimes have reversed word orders. Each line has sixteen syllables. The ending of each line of the poem shares the same rhyme.

The Autumnal Owl is a poetic form intended to teach a moral lesson concerning the concept of nature originally devised by the elf mimi Obscuredive. The form guides poets during improvised performances. The poem is a single quintain. The first line has twelve syllables. It has a terminal caesura. The second line has sixteen syllables. The third line has fourteen syllables. It has a medial caesura. The fourth line has twelve syllables. It has an initial caesura. The fifth line has seven syllables. It has a terminal caesura. The rhyme scheme of the poem is AAABB.

The Aquamarine Silkinesses is a light poetic form intended to express pleasure with a chosen subject which grew out of the performances of The Hatred of Haunting. The rules of the form are applied by poets to produce individual poems which can be recited. The poem is divided into three distinct parts: a couplet, a quintain and two tercets. Use of metaphor is characteristic of the form. [B]The first part concerns the past. Certain lines present different views of the same subject. It has lines with five syllables. The rhyme scheme respecting the full poem is AA. [B]The second part concerns current events. The fifth line of the quintain presents a different view of the subject of the first line. It has lines with eight syllables. The rhyme scheme respecting the full poem is BCBCB. [B]The third part concerns the future. Certain lines present different views of the same subject. It has lines with eight syllables. The rhyme scheme repeating in each stanza is aab.

musical_form.description: The Venerable Flutes is a form of music used to commemorate important events originating in The Playful Dyes. The rules of the form are applied by composers to produce individual pieces of music which can be performed. The music is played on a zurs—l and a arƒl. The musical voices are joined in melody. The entire performance is at a hurried pace. The melody has long phrases throughout the form. It is performed using the feb scale and in the ƒtrid rhythm. [B]The zurs—l always does the main melody and should be bright. [B]The arƒl always does the main melody and should evoke tears. [B]The Venerable Flutes has the following structure: a passage and an additional passage possibly all repeated. [B]The first simple passage is to be very loud. The zurs—l is confined to the raucous high register. Chords are packed close together in dense clusters in this passage. [B]The second simple passage is to be very soft. The zurs—l ranges from the buzzy low register to the strident middle register. This passage is richly layered with full chords making use of the available range. [B]Scales are constructed from twelve notes spaced evenly throughout the octave. The tonic note is fixed only at the time of performance. [B]The feb heptatonic scale is thought of as two disjoint chords spanning a tritone and a perfect fourth. These chords are named bidok and em„r. [B]The bidok tetrachord is the 1st, the 3rd, the 6th and the 7th degrees of the semitone octave scale. [B]The em„r tetrachord is the 8th, the 10th, the 12th and the 13th (completing the octave) degrees of the semitone octave scale. [B]The ƒtrid rhythm is made from three patterns: the tarmid, the lakish and the erong. [B]The tarmid rhythm is a single line with three beats. The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| - x x | [B]where x is a beat, - is silent and | indicates a bar. [B]The lakish rhythm is a single line with three beats. The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| x - x | [B]where x is a beat, - is silent and | indicates a bar. [B]The erong rhythm is a single line with three beats. The beats are named osed (spoken os), lanlar (la) and udir (ud). The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| X x x | [B]where X marks an accented beat, x is a beat and | indicates a bar.

The Flute of Rhythm is a form of music used for entertainment originating in The Playful Dyes. The rules of the form are applied by composers to produce individual pieces of music which can be performed. The music is played on three mukar and a arƒl. The musical voices bring melody with harmony. The entire performance is to be moderately soft. The melody has short phrases throughout the form. Chords, seldom-used, are sparse -- intervals and single pitches are favored. It is performed using the gost scale and in the kogan rhythm. [B]Each mukar always does the main melody. The voice stays in the quavering low register. [B]The arƒl always does harmony. [B]The Flute of Rhythm has a simple structure: three brief unrelated passages. [B]Each of the simple passages should be fiery and is very slow. [B]Scales are constructed from twelve notes spaced evenly throughout the octave. The tonic note is fixed only at the time of performance. [B]The gost heptatonic scale is thought of as two disjoint chords spanning a tritone and a perfect fourth. These chords are named nicol and em„r. [B]The nicol tetrachord is the 1st, the 2nd, the 6th and the 7th degrees of the semitone octave scale. [B]The em„r tetrachord is the 8th, the 10th, the 12th and the 13th (completing the octave) degrees of the semitone octave scale. [B]The kogan rhythm is made from two patterns: the lisig and the et„g. The patterns are to be played over the same period of time, concluding together regardless of beat number. [B]The lisig rhythm is a single line with thirty-two beats divided into five bars in a 10-7-6-5-4 pattern. The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| x x x x X x x x x x | x x x x X x - | - x X x - x | x - x X x | - x - - | [B]where X marks an accented beat, x is a beat, - is silent and | indicates a bar. [B]The et„g rhythm is a single line with seven beats. The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| X x x x - x x | [B]where X marks an accented beat, x is a beat, - is silent and | indicates a bar.

The Sheen of Sisters is a devotional form of music originating in The Playful Dyes. The rules of the form are applied by composers to produce individual pieces of music which can be performed. A chanter recites a composition of The Mother of Droplets while the music is played on a r¡bar and a rthar. The musical voices bring melody with harmony. The entire performance should be fiery. The melody has mid-length phrases throughout the form. It is performed using the bem•ng scale. Throughout, when possible, composers and performers are to use mordents, modulate frequently and play staccato. [B]The chanter always does the main melody. [B]The r¡bar always does harmony. [B]The rthar always does the main melody and plays arpeggios. [B]The Sheen of Sisters has the following structure: a theme and one to two series of variations on the theme possibly all repeated. [B]The theme is consistently slowing, and it is to be loud. The chanter's voice stays in the low register and the r¡bar covers its entire range from the fluid low register to the wavering high register. This passage is richly layered with full chords making use of the available range. The passage is performed in free rhythm. [B]Each of the series of variations is slower than the last passage, and it is to become softer and softer. The chanter's voice ranges from the middle register to the high register and the r¡bar stays in the fluid low register. This passage features only melodic tones and intervals. Each passage is performed in the s krith rhythm. [B]Scales are constructed from twelve notes spaced evenly throughout the octave. The tonic note is fixed only at the time of performance. [B]The bem•ng hexatonic scale is thought of as two disjoint chords spanning a tritone and a perfect fourth. These chords are named nicol and sedil. [B]The nicol tetrachord is the 1st, the 2nd, the 6th and the 7th degrees of the semitone octave scale. [B]The sedil trichord is the 8th, the 10th and the 13th (completing the octave) degrees of the semitone octave scale. [B]The s krith rhythm is made from two patterns: the et„g and the ibruk. The patterns are to be played over the same period of time, concluding together regardless of beat number. [B]The et„g rhythm is a single line with seven beats. The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| X x x x - x x | [B]where X marks an accented beat, x is a beat, - is silent and | indicates a bar. [B]The ibruk rhythm is a single line with thirty-two beats divided into eight bars in a 4-4-4-4-4-4-4-4 pattern. The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| - x X x | x - x - | - - x - | x - x - | - x - - | x - - - | - - x - | X - x x | [B]where X marks an accented beat, x is a beat, - is silent and | indicates a bar.

The Cardinal Wisps is a form of music used during marches and military engagements originating in The Playful Dyes. The form guides musicians during improvised performances. A chanter recites nonsensical words and sounds while the music is played on a kan. The musical voices are joined in melody. The entire performance should be made with feeling. The melody has long phrases throughout the form. It is performed using the ”ntak scale and in the nashon rhythm. Throughout, when possible, performers are to play rapid runs and alternate tension and repose. [B]The chanter always does the main melody. [B]The kan always does the main melody. [B]The Cardinal Wisps has the following structure: a passage and an additional passage possibly all repeated. [B]The first simple passage slows and broadens, and it is to become louder and louder. The chanter's voice stays in the high register. This passage features only melodic tones and intervals. [B]The second simple passage is half the tempo of the last passage, and it is to be soft. The chanter's voice ranges from the middle register to the high register. Only one pitch is ever played at a time in this passage. [B]Scales are constructed from twelve notes spaced evenly throughout the octave. The tonic note is fixed only at the time of performance. [B]The ”ntak hexatonic scale is thought of as two disjoint chords spanning a tritone and a perfect fourth. These chords are named alak and gatal. [B]The alak trichord is the 1st, the 5th and the 7th degrees of the semitone octave scale. [B]The gatal tetrachord is the 8th, the 9th, the 10th and the 13th (completing the octave) degrees of the semitone octave scale. [B]The nashon rhythm is made from three patterns: the fer, the erong and the asdos. The patterns are to be played over the same period of time, concluding together regardless of beat number. [B]The fer rhythm is a single line with seven beats. The beats are named uvel (spoken uv), dolush (do), agˆk (ag), ucat (uc), ng rak (ng ), enir (en) and ugath (ug). The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| x X x x x x x | [B]where X marks an accented beat, x is a beat and | indicates a bar. [B]The erong rhythm is a single line with three beats. The beats are named osed (spoken os), lanlar (la) and udir (ud). The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| X x x | [B]where X marks an accented beat, x is a beat and | indicates a bar. [B]The asdos rhythm is a single line with seven beats. The beats are named roder (spoken ro), nel (ne), biban (bi), ugog (ug), ish (ish), olmul (ol) and nokzam (no). The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| - - - - x - - | [B]where x is a beat, - is silent and | indicates a bar.

The Musical Rhythm is a form of music used during marches and military engagements originating in The Playful Dyes. The rules of the form are applied by composers to produce individual pieces of music which can be performed. Two chanters recite a composition of The Poetic Skirt while the music is played on a zeg and a gekur. The music is melody and rhythm without harmony. The entire performance should feel mysterious. The melody has short phrases throughout the form. It is performed using the izeg scale and in free rhythm. Throughout, when possible, composers and performers are to modulate frequently. [B]Each chanter always provides the rhythm. [B]The zeg always does the main melody. [B]The gekur always provides the rhythm. [B]The Musical Rhythm has a well-defined multi-passage structure: a theme, an exposition of the theme, a brief bridge-passage and a recapitulation of the theme. [B]The theme is at a hurried pace, and it is to become louder and louder. The zeg covers its entire range from the buzzy low register to the slicing high register and each of the chanters' voices covers its entire range. Only one pitch is ever played at a time in this passage. [B]The exposition is fast, and it is to be loud. The zeg covers its entire range from the buzzy low register to the slicing high register and each of the chanters' voices stays in the low register. This passage features only melodic tones and intervals. [B]The bridge-passage is consistently slowing, and it is to fade into silence. The zeg covers its entire range from the buzzy low register to the slicing high register and each of the chanters' voices stays in the middle register. This passage typically has some sparse chords. [B]The recapitulation slows and broadens, and it is to be in whispered undertones. The zeg stays in the slicing high register and each of the chanters' voices ranges from the middle register to the high register. This passage features only melodic tones and intervals. [B]Scales are constructed from twelve notes spaced evenly throughout the octave. The tonic note is fixed only at the time of performance. [B]The izeg heptatonic scale is thought of as two disjoint chords spanning a tritone and a perfect fourth. These chords are named nicol and mabdug. [B]The nicol tetrachord is the 1st, the 2nd, the 6th and the 7th degrees of the semitone octave scale. [B]The mabdug tetrachord is the 8th, the 10th, the 11th and the 13th (completing the octave) degrees of the semitone octave scale.

The Avalanche of Gravel is a devotional form of music directed toward the worship of £tost originating in The Playful Dyes. The rules of the form are applied by composers to produce individual pieces of music which can be performed. A singer recites nonsensical words and sounds. The melody has phrases of varied length throughout the form. Only one pitch is ever played at a time. It is performed using the berim scale and in the bugsud rhythm. Throughout, when possible, composers and performers are to play arpeggios. [B]The singer always does the main melody and should feel mysterious. [B]The Avalanche of Gravel has a well-defined multi-passage structure: a theme, a lengthy bridge-passage and one to two series of variations on the theme. [B]The theme is at a walking pace, and it is to be very loud. The singer's voice covers its entire range. The passage should be composed and performed using legato. [B]The bridge-passage accelerates as it proceeds, and it is to be moderately loud. The singer's voice covers its entire range. The passage should be composed and performed using legato. [B]Each of the series of variations is very fast, and it is to be very soft. The singer's voice ranges from the low register to the middle register. [B]Scales are constructed from twelve notes spaced evenly throughout the octave. The tonic note is fixed only at the time of performance. [B]The berim pentatonic scale is thought of as two disjoint chords spanning a tritone and a perfect fourth. These chords are named alak and sedil. [B]The alak trichord is the 1st, the 5th and the 7th degrees of the semitone octave scale. [B]The sedil trichord is the 8th, the 10th and the 13th (completing the octave) degrees of the semitone octave scale. [B]The bugsud rhythm is made from two patterns: the ibruk and the asdos. The patterns are to be played over the same period of time, concluding together regardless of beat number. [B]The ibruk rhythm is a single line with thirty-two beats divided into eight bars in a 4-4-4-4-4-4-4-4 pattern. The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| - x X x | x - x - | - - x - | x - x - | - x - - | x - - - | - - x - | X - x x | [B]where X marks an accented beat, x is a beat, - is silent and | indicates a bar. [B]The asdos rhythm is a single line with seven beats. The beats are named roder (spoken ro), nel (ne), biban (bi), ugog (ug), ish (ish), olmul (ol) and nokzam (no). The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| - - - - x - - | [B]where x is a beat, - is silent and | indicates a bar.

The Zephyr of Sheens is a form of music used during marches and military engagements originating in The Confederacy of Heart. The rules of the form are applied by composers to produce individual pieces of music which can be performed. The music is played on two c kuth and a ebi. The musical voices join in melody and counterpoint, harmony and rhythm. The entire performance should be made with feeling. The melody has long phrases, while the counterpoint has phrases of varied length throughout the form. It is performed using the nek scale and in the sut rhythm. Throughout, when possible, composers and performers are to use grace notes, alternate tension and repose and play staccato. The voice uses its entire range from the flat low register to the crisp high register. [B]The ebi always does the main melody. [B]The Zephyr of Sheens has a well-defined multi-passage structure: an introduction, one to two lengthy passages and an additional lengthy passage and a coda. [B]The introduction is voiced by the melody of the ebi and the harmony of the c kuth. The passage slows and broadens, and it is to be loud. Only one pitch is ever played at a time in this passage. [B]Each of the first simple passages is voiced by the melody of the c kuth and the melody of the ebi. Each passage is very slow, and it is to be in whispered undertones. Only one pitch is ever played at a time in this passage. [B]The second simple passage is voiced by the melody of the ebi and the counterpoint of the c kuth. The passage is at a free tempo, and it is to start loud then be immediately soft. This passage features only melodic tones and intervals. [B]The coda is voiced by the melody of the ebi and the rhythm of the c kuth. The passage is very slow, and it is to be moderately loud. Only one pitch is ever played at a time in this passage. [B]Scales are constructed from twenty-four notes spaced evenly throughout the octave. The tonic note is a fixed tone passed from teacher to student. Preferred notes in the fundamental scale are named. The names are ani (spoken an, 2nd), shato (sha, 7th), almef (al, 9th), o¤od (o¤, 10th), osp (osp, 15th), arin (ar, 17th), umo (um, 19th), rostfen (ro, 20th), hi¤er (hi, 22nd) and ohe (oh, 23rd). [B]The nek pentatonic scale is thought of as two disjoint chords spanning a perfect fifth and a major third. These chords are named rom and idla. [B]The rom trichord is the 1st, the 5th and the 15th degrees of the quartertone octave scale. [B]The idla trichord is the 17th, the 20th and the 25th (completing the octave) degrees of the quartertone octave scale. [B]The sut rhythm is made from two patterns: the cadem (considered the primary) and the apu. The patterns are to be played over the same period of time, concluding together regardless of beat number. [B]The cadem rhythm is a single line with three beats. The beats are named caquot (spoken ca), shibbi (shi) and aro (ar). The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| - x x | [B]where x is a beat, - is silent and | indicates a bar. [B]The apu rhythm is a single line with sixteen beats divided into two bars in a 8-8 pattern. The beats are named sluste (spoken slu), itlud (it), eman (em), oth (oth), ushav (us), asri (as), odu (od) and ijat (ij). The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| x - - x - - - - | x x x'- x x - x | [B]where ' marks a beat as late, x is a beat, - is silent and | indicates a bar.

The Festival of Poems is a devotional form of music originating in The Confederacy of Heart. The form guides musicians during improvised performances. Two to five singers recite a composition of The Sweet String while the music is played on a pod and a c kuth. The music is melody and rhythm without harmony. The entire performance should be made with feeling. The melody has phrases of varied length throughout the form. It is performed using the nithros scale and in free rhythm. Throughout, when possible, performers are to use mordents, play rapid runs, locally improvise and play legato. From beginning to end, when improvising, artists should sometimes include a falling melody pattern with flattened third degree, often include a rising melody pattern with trills and often include a rising-falling melody pattern. [B]Each singer always plays arpeggios. [B]The c kuth always does the main melody. The voice uses its entire range from the flat low register to the crisp high register. [B]The Festival of Poems has the following structure: a passage and an additional lengthy passage possibly all repeated. [B]The first simple passage is voiced by the melody of the c kuth, the rhythm of the singers and the rhythm of the pod. The passage is at a walking pace, and it is to be in whispered undertones. The c kuth covers its entire range from the flat low register to the crisp high register and each of the singers' voices stays in the high register. This passage typically has some sparse chords. [B]The second simple passage is voiced by the melody of the singers, the melody of the pod and the melody of the c kuth. The passage is at a walking pace, and it is to be very loud. Each of the singers' voices covers its entire range and the c kuth covers its entire range from the flat low register to the crisp high register. This passage is richly layered with full chords making use of the available range. [B]Scales are constructed from twenty-four notes spaced evenly throughout the octave. The tonic note is a fixed tone passed from teacher to student. Preferred notes in the fundamental scale are named. The names are ani (spoken an, 2nd), shato (sha, 7th), almef (al, 9th), o¤od (o¤, 10th), osp (osp, 15th), arin (ar, 17th), umo (um, 19th), rostfen (ro, 20th), hi¤er (hi, 22nd) and ohe (oh, 23rd). [B]The nithros hexatonic scale is thought of as two disjoint chords spanning a perfect fifth and a major third. These chords are named kasmko and woge. [B]The kasmko tetrachord is the 1st, the 7th, the 8th and the 15th degrees of the quartertone octave scale. [B]The woge trichord is the 17th, the 24th and the 25th (completing the octave) degrees of the quartertone octave scale.

The Glosses of Phrasing is a form of music used to commemorate important events originating in The Confederacy of Heart. The form guides musicians during improvised performances. Two speakers recite nonsensical words and sounds while the music is played on a pod. The musical voices are joined in melody. The melody has short phrases throughout the form. The music repeats for as long as necessary. It is performed using the cish scale. Throughout, when possible, performers are to glide from note to note. [B]Each speaker always should perform expressively and is to fade into silence. [B]The pod always does the main melody, should be delicate and is to be soft. [B]The Glosses of Phrasing has a well-defined multi-passage structure: a lengthy verse and a chorus all repeated up to two times, a brief bridge-passage, a verse and a chorus and a brief coda. [B]The first verse is moderately paced. Chords are packed close together in dense clusters in this passage. The passage is performed in free rhythm. The passage should be performed using arpeggios. [B]The first chorus is slow. This passage is richly layered with full chords making use of the available range. The passage is performed in the birta rhythm. The passage should be performed using arpeggios. [B]The bridge-passage is slower than the last passage. This passage typically has some sparse chords. The passage is performed in the stral rhythm. [B]The second verse resumes the previous tempo. This passage is richly layered with full chords making use of the available range. The passage is performed in the iquob rhythm. The passage should be performed using arpeggios. [B]The second chorus is at a free tempo. Chords are packed close together in dense clusters in this passage. The passage is performed in the cadem rhythm. [B]The coda is at a free tempo. This passage typically has some sparse chords. The passage is performed in the nazweng rhythm. The passage should be performed using arpeggios. [B]Scales are constructed from twenty-four notes spaced evenly throughout the octave. The tonic note is a fixed tone passed from teacher to student. Preferred notes in the fundamental scale are named. The names are ani (spoken an, 2nd), shato (sha, 7th), almef (al, 9th), o¤od (o¤, 10th), osp (osp, 15th), arin (ar, 17th), umo (um, 19th), rostfen (ro, 20th), hi¤er (hi, 22nd) and ohe (oh, 23rd). [B]The cish pentatonic scale is thought of as two disjoint chords spanning a perfect fifth and a major third. These chords are named use and woge. [B]The use trichord is the 1st, the 13th and the 15th degrees of the quartertone octave scale. [B]The woge trichord is the 17th, the 24th and the 25th (completing the octave) degrees of the quartertone octave scale. [B]The birta rhythm is made from three patterns: the apu (considered the primary), the leto and the stral. The patterns are to be played in the same beat, allowing one to repeat before the other is concluded. [B]The apu rhythm is a single line with sixteen beats divided into two bars in a 8-8 pattern. The beats are named sluste (spoken slu), itlud (it), eman (em), oth (oth), ushav (us), asri (as), odu (od) and ijat (ij). The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| x - - x - - - - | x x x'- x x - x | [B]where ' marks a beat as late, x is a beat, - is silent and | indicates a bar. [B]The leto rhythm is a single line with three beats. The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| x - - | [B]where x is a beat, - is silent and | indicates a bar. [B]The stral rhythm is a single line with two beats. The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| x - | [B]where x is a beat, - is silent and | indicates a bar. [B]The iquob rhythm is a single line with eighteen beats divided into two bars in a 11-7 pattern. The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| - x`- x x - x x - x - | - x - x - - - | [B]where ` marks a beat as early, x is a beat, - is silent and | indicates a bar. [B]The cadem rhythm is a single line with three beats. The beats are named caquot (spoken ca), shibbi (shi) and aro (ar). The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| - x x | [B]where x is a beat, - is silent and | indicates a bar. [B]The nazweng rhythm is a single line with five beats. The beats are named tod (spoken to), zomuth (zo), bepa (be), noloc (no) and kes (ke). The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| x x x x - | [B]where x is a beat, - is silent and | indicates a bar.

The Musical Chants is a form of music used for entertainment originating in The Confederacy of Heart. The form guides musicians during improvised performances. A singer recites a composition of The Dyes of Turquoise while the music is played on a pod and a c kuth. The musical voices bring melody, counterpoint and rhythm. The entire performance is fast. The melody and counterpoint both have mid-length phrases throughout the form. The music is broadly layered with chords spanning the range. It is performed using the ozi scale and in the thothil rhythm. Throughout, when possible, performers are to use grace notes, play staccato and match notes and syllables. [B]The singer always should feel agitated. [B]The pod always should perform with skill. [B]The c kuth always does the main melody and should feel mournful. The voice stays in the flat low register. [B]The Musical Chants has the following structure: a verse and a chorus all repeated up to two times. [B]The verse is voiced by the melody of the pod, the melody of the c kuth and the counterpoint of the singer. The passage is to fade into silence.
